about.title: Oakley Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Oakley residents rely on nearby Contra Costa County clinics, urgent care centers, and hospitals for everything from routine checkups to emergency surgery. Most visits go fine, but when a provider misses a diagnosis, makes a surgical error, or mismanages medication, the fallout can affect a person's health for years. Medical malpractice cases are different from a typical injury claim: California law requires a qualified medical expert to review the case and confirm that the care fell below an accepted standard, not just that the outcome was disappointing. There are also strict notice and filing deadlines unique to these claims. If you or someone in your family in Oakley was harmed by a medical error, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney experienced in these cases. The consultation is free, and there's no obligation to move forward. You'll have a chance to ask questions and understand your options before deciding anything.

items.title: Deadlines Are Strict and Case-Specific
items.desc: California generally allows one year from when you discovered the harm, but never more than three years from the injury itself, and a 90-day pre-suit notice is often required first. Missing these windows can end a claim before it starts, so timing matters.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Needed
items.desc: A bad medical outcome alone doesn't prove malpractice under California law; a qualified medical expert typically has to confirm the care fell below the accepted standard. An attorney experienced in these cases knows how to secure that kind of review.

items.title: Damages Caps Change Over Time
items.desc: California's cap on non-economic damages in medical malpractice cases rises each year by statute. Understanding how that cap applies to your situation is something an independent attorney can walk you through directly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim in Oakley?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA rules, you generally have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from the date it occurred. A 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider is usually required before filing. Because these deadlines are unforgiving, it helps to talk with an attorney as soon as you suspect something went wrong.

items.question: Is a poor medical outcome automatically considered malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law requires proof that a provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, not simply that the result was disappointing or unexpected. This is why a qualified medical expert almost always has to review the records first. An independent attorney can help arrange that kind of evaluation.

items.question: Do I need to have been treated at a specific Oakley facility to get help?
items.answer: No. Whether your care happened at a clinic, urgent care center, or hospital in or near Oakley, in Contra Costa County or elsewhere, LawProactive can still work to connect you with an independent attorney who handles these claims. What matters most is the medical care itself, not the exact location where it happened.
